featured.title: Oracle Just Told the SEC That AI Cost 21,000 Jobs. India Took More Than Half of Them.
featured.excerpt: The most candid admission yet that AI is replacing tech workers came in a regulatory filing — and roughly 12,000 of the cuts landed in India, where Oracle's largest workforce sits.
featured.image_caption: Servers in a data center, the infrastructure Oracle is spending tens of billions to expand even as it cuts staff
featured.nri_angle: Oracle is the first major tech firm to put AI job losses in writing to regulators, and with India absorbing the largest share, it is a warning shot for every Indian engineer on an H-1B watching the same companies spend on data centers while thinning their ranks.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Kohli's Name Is on India's England Squad. Whether He Boards the Plane Is Another Question.
news.excerpt: The BCCI has named a 15-man ODI squad for next month's tour of England, with Shubman Gill leading, Jasprit Bumrah back, and Virat Kohli picked subject to a fitness check on the hamstring that troubled him in the IPL final — a selection the diaspora will be watching closer than most.
news.image_caption: Virat Kohli, whose inclusion in India's ODI squad for the England tour is subject to a fitness check on a hamstring strain from the IPL 2026 final
news.nri_angle: An India tour of England is a home-from-home event for Britain's large Indian-origin community, turning grounds like Edgbaston and Old Trafford into seas of blue, while diaspora fans across North America and the Gulf watch through the night — and Kohli's fitness saga, Gill's new captaincy and the road to the 2027 World Cup make every selection call matter to millions.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Isn't at the World Cup. But Three Players of Indian Descent Are.
news.excerpt: For the first time, three footballers of Indian heritage — New Zealand's Sarpreet Singh, Qatar's Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid and Australia's Nishan Velupillay — are playing at a men's World Cup simultaneously, carrying a diaspora's story onto the sport's biggest stage even as India watches from the outside.
news.image_caption: Sarpreet Singh, the New Zealand midfielder born in Auckland to a family from Jalandhar, Punjab — believed to be the first Sikh footballer at a men's World Cup
news.nri_angle: For a diaspora of some 35 million that has never seen India at a men's World Cup, the simultaneous presence of three Indian-origin players — a Punjabi Sikh for New Zealand, a Gulf-born Malayali for Qatar, and a South-Asian-heritage winger for Australia — is both a source of pride and a pointed reminder of the talent India fails to develop at home, making the 2026 tournament a uniquely personal watch for Indians worldwide.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Newest Mega-Airport Is About to Send Its First Plane Abroad. The Destination Is Abu Dhabi.
news.excerpt: On July 15, Air India Express will fly Navi Mumbai International Airport's maiden international service to Abu Dhabi — the moment a greenfield giant meant to relieve Mumbai's choked skies joins the global map, and a new door home for the Gulf's vast Indian workforce.
news.image_caption: An Air India Express aircraft; the airline will operate Navi Mumbai International Airport's first international flight, to Abu Dhabi, on July 15
news.nri_angle: For the Gulf's vast Indian workforce — the UAE hosts one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities and a major source of India's record remittances — Navi Mumbai's first international flight opens another, less-congested gateway home and is set to deepen the Mumbai-to-Abu Dhabi ties of investment, family travel and business that define modern diaspora life.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Trump's Trade Envoy Has Left Delhi. India Says the Two Sides Are Now Mapping the Way to a Deal.
news.excerpt: Two days of talks between US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal ended Wednesday with both governments calling it 'substantial progress' — and Washington saying the long-promised deal is 'very, very close.' What India wants is a tariff edge over its rivals before a July 24 clock runs out.
news.image_caption: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who led India's side of the two-day trade talks with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: For the millions of Indian-Americans and the diaspora-run importers, distributors and tech firms that straddle both economies, the tariff line in this deal decides whether Indian-made goods stay competitive on US shelves and whether the talent-mobility and digital-trade chapters ease the careers of engineers and founders working across Silicon Valley and India — with a July 24 deadline raising the stakes of getting it done.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Two Decades of Talking, India and Europe Finally Have a Date. The 'Mother of All Deals' Gets Signed by December.
news.excerpt: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says the India-EU free-trade pact will be signed by December and take effect by February or March 2027, opening nearly the entire European market to Indian exporters — and reshaping the economics for a diaspora that straddles both.
news.image_caption: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who confirmed the India-EU free-trade pact will be signed by December and take effect by early 2027
news.nri_angle: For the millions of people of Indian origin across Europe, the FTA promises cheaper costs and wider margins for diaspora-run businesses that trade Indian textiles, food and craft goods, more predictable export routes into a 450-million-consumer market, and clearer professional-mobility rules for skilled Indians eyeing the continent as US and UK routes grow uncertain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: China Just Got the WTO to Put India's 'Make in India' Solar Push on Trial
news.excerpt: Geneva's Dispute Settlement Body has agreed to set up a panel to examine India's tariffs and incentives for solar and IT goods, which Beijing says discriminate against Chinese products — a test case for how far India can go to build factories at home without breaking global trade rules.
news.image_caption: A solar installation; China has won a WTO panel to examine India's solar and IT-goods tariffs and incentives
news.nri_angle: The case puts 'Make in India' — the manufacturing drive that has drawn diaspora capital, returning engineers and NRI investors betting on Indian factories — on trial at the WTO, testing whether India can keep using tariffs and local-content incentives to build a China-alternative industrial base without breaking global trade rules.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Quietly Telling the Gulf to Pay Its 5 Million Workers More. It's a Billion-Dollar Bet With a Catch.
news.excerpt: Over the past several months, Indian diplomats across all six Gulf states have sharply raised the minimum salaries they recommend for Indian workers — a drive that could pull in billions more in remittances, but also risks pricing some of India's own citizens out of the market.
news.image_caption: Construction in the Gulf, where more than five million Indians work and remit billions home
news.nri_angle: More than five million Indians — the largest migrant group in the Gulf and the source of remittances that sustain countless households across Kerala, UP, Bihar and Tamil Nadu — stand to earn meaningfully more if India's push to raise minimum wages succeeds, but blue-collar workers are also the ones who could lose jobs if Gulf employers pivot to cheaper labour from rival nations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: On July 15, an Indian Professional Posted to Britain Stops Paying Twice for the Same Pension
news.excerpt: The India-UK free-trade pact, signed last year, finally goes live next month — and tucked inside it is a social-security carve-out that puts real money back in the pockets of Indians sent to work in Britain. Trade Minister Piyush Goyal flies to London this week to nail down the rollout.
news.image_caption: The City of London; the India-UK CETA free-trade pact comes into force on July 15, easing trade and professional mobility
news.nri_angle: Britain's 1.9-million-strong Indian community — and especially the IT engineers, consultants and managers posted there temporarily by Indian firms — gain real take-home pay from July 15, when the India-UK CETA's Double Contribution Convention stops them paying social security in both countries, while diaspora-run exporters get new openings into the British market.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: One of India's Biggest Automakers Woke Up to a Ransomware Attack. The Bigger Worry Is What It Signals.
news.excerpt: Bajaj Auto, the Pune-based maker of motorcycles and three-wheelers sold from Lagos to Los Angeles, says a ransomware attack hit its systems and those of its technology arm early on June 23. It calls its response successful so far — but the breach lands amid a wave of cyberattacks on India's industrial backbone.
news.image_caption: Bajaj Auto, the Pune-based maker of motorcycles and three-wheelers, disclosed a ransomware attack on its systems
news.nri_angle: Bajaj is a globally recognised Indian brand whose two- and three-wheelers are sold across the diaspora's home markets in Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and a stock many NRIs hold; a ransomware hit on so digitised a manufacturer is a warning sign about the cyber-resilience of the Indian industrial firms the diaspora invests in and takes pride in.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Britain Is About to Smash Its June Heat Record. For 1.9 Million Indians There, This Is a Safety Story.
news.excerpt: A Saharan 'heat dome' has pushed western Europe into a deadly, record-breaking heatwave. The UK Met Office has issued a rare red alert warning of a risk to life, schools are shutting and trains are cancelled — just as London hosts its flagship climate week and changes prime ministers.
news.image_caption: The City of London skyline; Britain is forecast to break its June heat record amid a rare Met Office red alert
news.nri_angle: Britain's 1.9 million people of Indian origin — concentrated in heat-exposed cities, often in older homes without air-conditioning, with elderly relatives in the at-risk group — are living through a record, potentially deadly heatwave, making this an urgent safety story for the UK and wider European diaspora, complete with the official guidance families need.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Their Lawmakers Have a Message for 5 Million Indian-Americans: Stop Being on the Menu, Get a Seat at the Table.
news.excerpt: At a Capitol Hill gathering, Congressmen Raja Krishnamoorthi, Suhas Subramanyam and Shri Thanedar urged Indian-Americans to run for office at every level as anti-Hindu and anti-India hate rises — a call for one of America's wealthiest and most-educated communities to convert economic clout into political power.
news.image_caption: Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, who urged Indian-Americans to run for office at every level
news.nri_angle: This is a direct call to the 5.2-million-strong Indian-American community to convert its economic and educational success into political representation, framed by its own elected lawmakers as the only durable defence against rising anti-Hindu and anti-India hate and against stalled priorities like the green-card backlog.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Will Now Let Its Banks Lend NRIs Money to Buy More Indian Deposits. The Returns Could Touch 15%.
news.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has cleared domestic lenders to extend loans to non-residents against their foreign-currency deposits — including through GIFT City — the final missing piece of a scheme designed to pull diaspora dollars in and prop up a weak rupee. Analysts say leverage could lift NRI returns toward 12-15 percent and draw in tens of billions.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India, which cleared banks to lend to NRIs against their foreign-currency deposits
news.nri_angle: This is aimed squarely at non-resident Indians: the RBI is now letting banks lend NRIs money against their own dollar deposits, a leverage loop that analysts say could push diaspora returns toward 12-15 percent while channelling tens of billions of overseas-Indian dollars back home to steady the rupee.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Mounting Its Biggest-Ever Security Operation for the Amarnath Pilgrimage. Here's Why This Year Is Different.
news.excerpt: Ahead of the 57-day Amarnath Yatra that begins July 3, the government has approved a record 670 companies of central forces — a multi-layered grid stretching from the Jammu gateway to the Himalayan cave shrine. For the diaspora that travels home for the pilgrimage, and for families across Kashmir, the scale of this year's deployment is unprecedented.
news.image_caption: Security personnel guard pilgrims at the Amarnath cave shrine in Jammu and Kashmir; this year India is mounting its largest-ever security operation for the Yatra (Wikimedia Commons).
news.nri_angle: The Amarnath Yatra draws NRIs who fly home each summer for the pilgrimage and is watched closely by the large Kashmiri and J&K-origin diaspora, so a record 670-company security deployment for the July 3-August 28 Yatra matters both as the safety guarantee that makes the trip possible and as a barometer of how their home region is being governed.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Becoming an American Is About to Get Much More Expensive. Indian Green-Card Holders Will Feel It First.
news.excerpt: A new Trump administration proposal would raise the cost of applying for US citizenship by up to 80 percent — from $710 to $1,280 online, and $760 to $1,330 on paper — while scrapping most fee waivers for low-income applicants. For the hundreds of thousands of Indians who form the largest single bloc of new American citizens, the math on naturalization just changed.
news.image_caption: A US naturalization ceremony; a new DHS proposal would raise citizenship application fees by up to 80 percent
news.nri_angle: Indians are consistently among the largest groups of new US citizens and the biggest bloc on employment-based green-card tracks, so a proposed 75-80% jump in the N-400 naturalization fee — toward roughly ₹1.26 lakh per applicant — plus the loss of low-income waivers directly raises the cost of the final step for hundreds of thousands of NRI families, with a 60-day comment window before any rule becomes final.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Six Decades, India Is Letting Private Money Into Its Nuclear Plants
news.excerpt: A landmark law has ended the state monopoly on atomic power, opening the sector to private operators and up to 49% foreign investment. New Delhi is chasing roughly $26 billion in private capital and a 100-gigawatt target — and a diaspora hungry for both clean-energy bets and a stake in India's rise is squarely in the frame.
news.image_caption: Technicians load fuel assemblies at the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant; India has opened the sector to private operators and foreign investment for the first time
news.nri_angle: The opening of India's nuclear sector gives overseas Indians a first-ever, ground-floor route into one of the country's biggest long-term infrastructure bets — a patient clean-energy play suited to diaspora capital, foreign partners and the many NRIs working in global nuclear, engineering and clean-tech — while answering a diaspora desire for Indian energy security after the recent Hormuz oil scare.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indians in the UAE Have a Five-Day Window to Sort Their Passports. Then Services Go Dark.
news.excerpt: The Indian Embassy is pausing all routine passport, visa and attestation work from June 26 to 30 as a new contractor, Al Hind Tours, replaces BLS and SGIVS from July 1. For the roughly 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the country's largest expatriate community — the message is simple: file now, or wait until July.
news.image_caption: An Indian Emergency Certificate, a consular travel document issued by Indian missions abroad; UAE consular services pause June 26-30 during a contractor handover
news.nri_angle: The UAE hosts India's single largest overseas community of roughly 3.5 million people, so a planned five-day pause in passport, visa and attestation services — with a hard June 25 filing deadline before Al Hind Tours replaces BLS and SGIVS on July 1 — directly affects thousands of NRI households, especially blue-collar workers whose jobs, tenancies and family visas hinge on timely consular paperwork.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ambani Just Filed the Paperwork for India's Biggest-Ever IPO. The Company Is Jio.
news.excerpt: Reliance has lodged draft papers to list Jio Platforms in Mumbai in an offering that could raise about $4 billion and value the business near $137 billion. For a diaspora that already touches Jio through Meta and Google's stakes, it is a rare chance to own a slice of the network that rewired India.
news.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed for India's largest-ever IPO
news.nri_angle: The Jio IPO gives overseas Indians a rare, direct way to own the network that rewired daily life back home — the cheap data behind their video calls, the rails behind their remittances, the streaming that keeps them tied to Indian cricket and cinema — and, through the NRI investor route, the listing will be a marquee test of whether diaspora appetite for Indian assets holds up in a jittery market.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Got Its First Sovereign-AI Unicorn. The Bigger Question Is Whether It's Building Fast Enough.
news.excerpt: Bengaluru's Sarvam has raised $234 million to build AI models from scratch in India, even as a Wall Street note warns the country risks letting foreign systems power its banks, defence and public services. For a diaspora that staffs the world's AI labs, the contest over who controls the models is suddenly personal.
news.image_caption: A data-center server hall; India is racing to build sovereign AI models trained at home
news.nri_angle: Indians and people of Indian origin run or sit near the top of nearly every major AI lab in the United States — the very talent that built the frontier models India now worries about depending on — so India's sovereign-AI push is an attempt to give that diaspora a reason to build at home or for home, even as many NRIs work for the Western labs whose dominance New Delhi is trying to reduce.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: ‘On the Menu’: Indian-American Lawmakers Tell the Diaspora to Stop Watching and Start Running for Office
nri-world.excerpt: At a Capitol Hill event, three Indian-American congressmen warned that economic success no longer buys political protection, and urged the community to seek power at every level of government.
nri-world.image_caption: Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, who urged Indian-Americans to run for public office at a FIIDS event on Capitol Hill.
nri-world.nri_angle: For a first-generation diaspora that arrived to study and work, these lawmakers are asking the community to trade quiet, private success for visible political power as anti-India and anti-Hindu incidents rise.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Gulf Was the Diaspora's Safe Haven. A War Is Forcing 9 Million Indians to Recalculate.
nri-world.excerpt: As conflict reshapes West Asia, Indian community networks have become a quiet backbone of mutual aid, even as the divide between the diaspora's professionals and its labourers grows starker.
nri-world.image_caption: The Dubai skyline at dusk; nearly 3.5 million Indians live and work in the United Arab Emirates.
nri-world.nri_angle: The Gulf holds the largest single bloc of overseas Indians and a pillar of India's $135bn in remittances; the war is testing both their physical safety and the unspoken bargain that drew them there.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Diaspora With No Homeland to Return To Is Trying to Build One in the Cloud
nri-world.excerpt: As Sindhis gather in Toronto this July, the community is attempting something it has rarely managed in 70 years of dispersal: a permanent global institution to hold itself together.
nri-world.image_caption: Members of the South Asian diaspora gather at a community cultural event.
nri-world.nri_angle: The Sindhis run the assimilation experiment without the safety net of a homeland, making their fight to preserve language and identity an accelerated preview of what every Indian diaspora community eventually faces.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: How a Single Sunday of Yoga Maps Britain's Indian Diaspora
nri-world.excerpt: From a Jain centre in Hertfordshire to a square in Birmingham, the 12th International Day of Yoga showed the organizing muscle, and the soft power, of a community.
nri-world.image_caption: Participants take part in a mass open-air session marking the International Day of Yoga.

sources.label: IANS — Indian missions worldwide mark International Day of Yoga
Oshwal Association of the U.K. — International Yoga Day 2026
United Nations — International Day of Yoga 2026

nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's coordinated Yoga Day celebrations reveal the Indian diaspora as both the original carrier of yoga to the West and a living infrastructure of community organizations now deploying it as cultural diplomacy.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: On Long Island, a Parade Becomes a Measure of How Far Indian-Americans Have Come
nri-world.excerpt: The curtain raiser for the 15th India Day Parade drew 250 people and a row of elected officials, evidence of a diaspora moving from enclave to mainstream.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian-Americans celebrate Independence Day with a flag-raising procession in New York.

sources.label: The Indian EYE — 15th India Day Parade USA 2026: Curtain Raiser Draws A Full House
The Indian EYE — IDP USA India Day Parade of Long Island

nri-world.nri_angle: The Long Island India Day Parade shows how a maturing Indian-American community converts cultural celebration into political visibility, while wrestling with how to pass its volunteer-built institutions to a second generation growing up American.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: In a Paris Concert Hall, Modi Recasts the Diaspora as India's Ambassadors Abroad
nri-world.excerpt: Addressing overseas Indians at the Salle Pleyel, the prime minister offered affection and a quiet argument: that the community is now an instrument of national influence.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a visit to France, where he addressed the Indian diaspora.

sources.label: The Indian EYE — PM Modi lauds diaspora as true strength of India-France ties
IANS — PM Modi given warm welcome by Indian diaspora in Paris: MEA
IANS — Paris is city of lights and colours: PM Modi to Indian diaspora

nri-world.nri_angle: Modi's Paris address crystallizes how his government has recast overseas Indians from emigrants who left into strategic 'Rashtradoots' expected to carry India's trade, technology and image into their adopted countries.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Ottawa and Delhi Barely Spoke for Two Years. This Week, 100 Companies Flew In to Change That.
nri-world.excerpt: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal led India's largest-ever business delegation to Canada — and cast the Indo-Canadian diaspora as the bridge that outlasted the diplomatic freeze.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who led the largest-ever Indian business delegation to Canada
nri-world.nri_angle: After two years caught in the India-Canada diplomatic crossfire, 1.8 million Indo-Canadians are being recast from a security headache into the relationship's most valuable asset as trade talks revive.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Stretch of the Jersey City Waterfront Vanished Under Colored Powder. For Thousands, It Was the Only Holi They Know.
nri-world.excerpt: Surati Holi Hai 2026 drew thousands to Exchange Place — a summer-scheduled spring festival that shows how the diaspora keeps tradition alive by replicating the feeling, not the calendar.
nri-world.image_caption: Revelers covered in colored powder at a Holi festival celebration
nri-world.nri_angle: For second-generation kids who have never seen Holi in India, the Jersey City festival is not a copy of home — it is the real thing, and the institution-building behind it is what turns a population into a community.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Taste of Home Used to Arrive in a Suitcase. Now It Has a Shelf in the Duty-Free Hall.
nri-world.excerpt: Premium Indian beverages have entered Canada's airport duty-free retail — a milestone built, one grocery run at a time, by 1.8 million Indo-Canadians.
nri-world.image_caption: An airport duty-free retail hall, where premium Indian products are now finding shelf space
nri-world.nri_angle: The generation that arrived with spice boxes wrapped in newspaper now watches its children pass Indian brands in the duty-free hall — the pantry that once marked them as outsiders has become a category the mainstream wants to sell.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Diaspora Famous for Sending Money Home Just Pledged $1 Million to Feed Americans Instead
nri-world.excerpt: The HungerMitao movement, built on the slogan 'give where you live,' is quietly redirecting Indian-American philanthropy toward the country the community actually lives in.
nri-world.image_caption: Volunteers pack food donations at the Capital Area Food Bank in the U.S. (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: HungerMitao reframes who the diaspora is responsible for — arguing an Indian-American shares a moral claim with a hungry neighbour in their own US city, not only with causes back in India. It is both a unifying force across a fragmented community and a statement of belonging.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Cricket Legend and a Blind Industrialist Walked Into a Charity Gala. The Diaspora Opened Its Wallet.
nri-world.excerpt: At the Sankara Eye Foundation's annual fundraiser, Sunil Gavaskar's autographed bats and Srikanth Bolla's life story turned nostalgia into surgeries for the blind back in India.
nri-world.image_caption: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar, who headlined the Sankara Eye Foundation's diaspora fundraising gala
nri-world.nri_angle: Diaspora philanthropy that funds free eye surgeries in India shows how NRI giving has institutionalised — audited charities, celebrity draws, named sponsor tiers — as a way for immigrants to stay tethered to home and pass that obligation to American-raised children.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Each Summer, a Building-Sized Chariot Rolls Down a North American Street. That's the Whole Point.
nri-world.excerpt: The Ratha Yatra has become the diaspora's most outward-facing ritual — staged on public streets from New York to Vancouver, designed for the neighbours who have never set foot in a temple.
nri-world.image_caption: Devotees pull a towering chariot during an ISKCON Ratha Yatra procession
nri-world.nri_angle: Unlike inward-looking diaspora gatherings, the Ratha Yatra is staged in public for a non-Indian audience — inverting the exclusivity of the Puri original, doing cheap and effective soft-power work, and giving American- and Canadian-raised children a sensory link to a tradition their parents left behind.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. The World Is Still Deciding Whether to Walk In.
markets-finance.excerpt: After scrapping the tax on foreign holdings of government bonds and widening access, India has lured early buyers — including a rare $1 billion bet by Canada's Fairfax — and is angling for a coveted Bloomberg index seat. But a weak rupee and steep hedging costs may yet keep the big money cautious.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's bond-market reforms aim to lure global investors as a weak rupee tests their appetite
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's push to pull global money into its government bonds runs on the same engine the diaspora is being courted with — dollar deposits, GIFT City, index inclusion — and the outcome will shape the yields, the rupee and the investment options NRIs see when they decide how much of their savings to send home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Opens a New Door to the World's Markets — and It Runs Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: A wave of new funds is letting Indians invest in US stocks and global assets through the country's tax-neutral financial hub, with the fund itself shouldering the tax — but the fine print on remittance limits and levies still rewards a careful reading.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian financial-district skyline; new funds based in GIFT City are opening fresh routes for Indians and NRIs to invest in global markets
markets-finance.nri_angle: GIFT City is being built explicitly to court the diaspora's capital, and for NRIs weighing how to hold global assets with an Indian foot, the new IFSC funds change the calculus on tax, repatriation and paperwork — exactly the friction points that have long made cross-border investing a headache.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — but This Time, the Marquee Backers Don't Get to Cash Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Reliance's digital arm has filed papers for a roughly $3.8 billion listing, with every rupee earmarked for debt and growth — meaning the Meta, Google and Gulf investors who poured in during 2020 will have to wait their turn.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Jio's headquarters. Jio Platforms has filed a draft prospectus for what would be India's largest-ever IPO.
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio's listing will be the marquee Indian IPO of a generation, and NRIs — long among the most eager retail buyers of marquee Indian names — will be weighing whether to chase it; the unusual all-fresh-issue structure and the holding-company discount are exactly the fine print diaspora investors need to read before committing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Wants to Grow at 10%. First It Has to Explain Why Foreign Investment Has Dried Up.
markets-finance.excerpt: Net foreign direct investment fell to just $7.7 billion last year — a fraction of Vietnam's and Indonesia's — and India's top industry lobby says slow courts and five-year arbitration waits are scaring off the capital the country needs.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's financial capital, Mumbai, where weak foreign direct investment is testing the country's growth ambitions
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs are among the most natural foreign investors in India — through direct stakes, startups and property — yet the same slow courts and tangled dispute resolution that deter global capital are exactly what burn diaspora investors who get stuck in years-long litigation back home, making this a story about whether India can finally be trusted with their money.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Tata Motors Bets on a Five-Year Turnaround — ₹6 Lakh Crore in Revenue, and a Promise to Clear Its Debt
markets-finance.excerpt: At its investor day, Tata Motors' passenger-vehicle group set out targets to lift consolidated revenue past ₹6 lakh crore and reach a 10% margin by FY31, and to be net debt-free by FY29 — even as a cautious JLR outlook for FY27 left brokerages split.
markets-finance.image_caption: Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover unit, maker of the Range Rover, anchors the group's five-year turnaround plan
markets-finance.nri_angle: Tata Motors is both a heavyweight in the Nifty and Sensex that anchor most NRI India portfolios and the owner of Jaguar Land Rover, whose Range Rovers and Defenders the diaspora actually buys on the streets of London, New Jersey and Toronto — making its five-year bet a rare stock where the diaspora is invested in the shares and the showroom at once.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India’s Economy Just Cooled to a Three-Month Low — and a Resurgent Dollar Is Squeezing the Rupee Again
markets-finance.excerpt: Fresh data show India’s private-sector growth slowing and business confidence at its weakest in nearly four years, just as rising bets on a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike push the dollar to a one-year high and drag the rupee and Indian stocks lower.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Indian markets pulled back as growth cooled and a stronger dollar pressured the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs, the twin pressures matter directly: a weaker rupee stretches the value of dollars sent home or invested in India, while a cooling economy and a hawkish Fed reshape the calculus on when to remit, when to buy Indian equities, and how much currency risk to carry.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Courting the Diaspora’s Dollars to Rescue the Rupee — and Banks Are Racing to Cash In
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI is subsidising hedging costs on foreign-currency deposits and now letting domestic banks lend against them, in a 2013-style push to pull tens of billions of NRI dollars into the country. Analysts estimate the scheme could draw anywhere from $55 billion to $100 billion.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India is courting diaspora dollars through high-yield foreign-currency deposits to defend the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This scheme is aimed squarely at NRIs: with banks now offering 6–7 percent on dollar deposits — and leveraged structures that could push returns toward 12–15 percent — overseas Indians can earn high rupee-equivalent yields without taking on currency risk, while helping defend the very rupee their families back home depend on.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Reliance Lays Out a Five-Year Plan to Double Its Earnings — With AI and the Sun at the Centre
markets-finance.excerpt: At its 49th AGM, Mukesh Ambani's conglomerate paired a record-profit year with bold targets: doubling consolidated EBITDA, a ₹1-trillion FMCG business, an AI push across every product, and 200,000 green-energy jobs — even as the stock trades well below its peak.
markets-finance.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani used Reliance's 49th AGM to set a five-year target of doubling the conglomerate's core earnings
markets-finance.nri_angle: Reliance is the single heaviest weight in the Sensex and Nifty that anchor most NRI India portfolios and mutual-fund SIPs, so its five-year bet on AI, consumer brands and solar energy is, in effect, a bet on the direction of the entire market the diaspora invests in — and a preview of where India's economy is trying to go.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Bought More Russian Oil Than Ever — Right as Washington's Sanctions Waiver Expires
markets-finance.excerpt: After the Iran war scrambled global energy flows, Russia's share of India's crude imports has nearly doubled to almost half, hitting a record 2.55 million barrels a day in June — but a lapsed US waiver now forces a tricky choice on Delhi's refiners.
markets-finance.image_caption: Russia now supplies almost half of India's crude imports, with a record 2.55 million barrels a day arriving in June
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's energy bill is the hidden hinge of its economy — it shapes inflation, the rupee NRIs send money in, and the stock indices the diaspora invests in — so how Delhi balances cheap Russian crude against renewed US sanctions pressure will ripple straight through the remittances and portfolios that tie the diaspora to home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An Accenture Warning Knocks Indian IT — and the Bigger Fear Is What It Signals for Next Year
markets-finance.excerpt: After the world's largest IT services firm trimmed its revenue outlook, Indian software giants like Infosys, TCS and Wipro slid as much as 7 percent, and brokerages warned that the coming financial year could prove tougher than the market has been pricing in.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian IT majors slid sharply after Accenture trimmed its revenue guidance, dragging the Nifty IT index lower
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's bellwether industry — it employs many NRIs' relatives, anchors the portfolios of those who invest back home, and underpins the H-1B pipeline that brought a generation to America — so a warning that demand and AI are squeezing the sector touches NRI jobs, savings and family fortunes at once.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Faces Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years — but This Time the Economy Is Better Armoured
markets-finance.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has delayed the rains and brought dangerous heat, threatening harvests, food prices and growth. Yet bigger reservoirs and far wider irrigation mean the damage may be more contained than the alarming headlines suggest.
markets-finance.image_caption: India faces its weakest monsoon in 11 years as a strengthening El Niño delays the rains and brings dangerous heat
markets-finance.nri_angle: A poor monsoon feeds straight into the things NRIs watch most closely about India — food inflation that erodes the rupee's value, the central bank's room to cut rates, and the strength of the currency their remittances and investments are denominated in — making this year's rains a quiet but real input into diaspora financial decisions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold Was Supposed to Soar During the Iran War. It Fell Nearly 10% Instead — Now JP Morgan Sees a 40% Rebound
markets-finance.excerpt: The metal that diaspora families trust as a crisis hedge defied its safe-haven reputation, sliding even as conflict raged, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams. The episode is a sharp lesson in how gold really behaves — and why timing it is a fool's errand.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold fell nearly 10% in India during the Iran war despite its safe-haven reputation, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's instinctive store of value — bought for weddings, gifted at festivals, hoarded as insurance against bad times — so its counter-intuitive slide during an actual war, and the debate over where it goes next, speaks directly to how NRIs should size and time their single most emotional investment.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Badminton's Biggest Stage Comes Home: India Hosts the World Championships for the First Time in 17 Years
sports.excerpt: Tickets are live for the BWF World Championships in New Delhi this August — and PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen and Satwik–Chirag will play a Worlds on home soil for the first time in their careers.
sports.image_caption: India's PV Sindhu, the country's most decorated player at the BWF World Championships, headlines the home field in New Delhi this August.
sports.nri_angle: After cricket, badminton is the sport the Indian diaspora follows most closely — and PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen and Satwik–Chirag are household names in NRI homes abroad. A home World Championships in mid-August, with global ticketing on BookMyShow, lands in the NRI summer-travel window and is exactly the kind of fixed-date event diaspora families plan an India trip around.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Finally Gave Its Track Stars a Night of Their Own — and Neeraj Chopra Owned It
sports.excerpt: At the inaugural Indian Athletics Awards in New Delhi, the Olympic javelin champion was named Best Male Athlete of 2025 — hours after flying in from his injury comeback in Doha — as India's federation set out to build a culture of recognition for the sport it now wins at beyond cricket.
sports.image_caption: Olympic javelin champion Neeraj Chopra, named Best Male Athlete of the Year 2025 at the inaugural Indian Athletics Awards in New Delhi.
sports.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is the rare Indian sporting icon who is not a cricketer — the most globally recognized face of India's Olympic ambitions and a unifying figure the diaspora follows from Tokyo to Paris. India's first-ever athletics awards night signals the country building institutions of recognition for track and field, the discipline diaspora children actually compete in at schools and colleges across the US, UK and Canada — and Chopra's message that Indians can match the world's best speaks directly to those kids.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Just Hosted Asia's Biggest Fencing Event for the First Time. Its Brightest Star Left With a Suspension.
sports.excerpt: The Asian Senior Fencing Championships came to New Delhi this week — a milestone for an Olympic sport India is only beginning to build — but a black card for Bhavani Devi, the country's first Olympic fencer, cast a shadow over the breakthrough.
sports.image_caption: Bhavani Devi, India's first Olympic fencer, in competition. A black card at the Asian Championships in New Delhi earned her a two-month suspension.
sports.nri_angle: Fencing is a European and East-Asian sport by tradition, but in the US, UK and Canada it is an established school and college sport and an Ivy League recruiting pathway — something many diaspora families know far better than relatives back home. India hosting the Asian Senior Fencing Championships for the first time, led by its one global star Bhavani Devi, is a bridge between the sport the diaspora lives with abroad and the country it came from.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Has Never Had a Sprinter Like Animesh Kujur. Now He's Heading to the Commonwealth Games.
sports.excerpt: The 23-year-old from Odisha holds the national records in both the 100m and 200m — the sport's glamour events, where India has never belonged — and a season of international podiums has booked his ticket to Glasgow.
sports.image_caption: Animesh Kujur, India's national record holder in the 100m and 200m, competing at the 2025 World University Games.
sports.nri_angle: Sprinting's blue-riband 100m and 200m have always belonged to the Caribbean, the US and West Africa — India has never figured. For diaspora fans in the US, UK and Canada who tune into track only at the Olympics, an Indian man running 10.1 and 20.3 and now lining up at the Commonwealth Games is a genuinely new kind of representation in the sport's glamour events.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A 7-Foot-4 Teenager From Punjab Has the NBA Internet Calling India Its Next 'Wemby'
sports.excerpt: Jagmeet Singh, an 18-year-old big man from Hoshiarpur, went viral after a prospect camp in the United States — and for a country that has never produced an NBA draftee through the traditional pipeline, the hype is its own kind of milestone.
sports.image_caption: A young Indian player trains at the NBA Basketball School in New Delhi; India's NBA development pipeline has been building for a decade (representative image).
sports.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in the US and Canada — where basketball, not cricket, is the sport their kids grow up playing — a 7-foot-4 Punjabi teenager being compared to Victor Wembanyama is a rare moment of representation in a North American game, and the buzz is loudest in the very camps and AAU circuits where diaspora families already live.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: England Name Their Squad for India — and a World Cup Score to Settle at Home
sports.excerpt: Beaten by India in the T20 World Cup semifinal, England have picked a 17-man squad for a five-match home series starting July 1, keeping faith with Jos Buttler and handing Sussex's James Coles a maiden call-up — the start of a white-ball summer that will fill Old Trafford and Trent Bridge with the diaspora.
sports.image_caption: Harry Brook, who will captain England in the five-match home T20I series against India starting July 1, 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
sports.nri_angle: The five-match T20I series lands at grounds with some of the largest British-Indian crowds in world cricket — Old Trafford, Trent Bridge, Edgbaston — and is the first India-England meeting since India ended England's home T20 World Cup in the semifinal, putting a ticketed revenge narrative on the diaspora's doorstep across England this July.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Sprinters Beat China for Relay Gold — a Statement Beyond the Javelin
sports.excerpt: At the Asian Relays Championships in Shangyu, India's women's 4x100m quartet ran down the host nation for gold, and a mixed-relay silver and bronze signalled that the country's track ambitions are spreading well past Neeraj Chopra.
sports.image_caption: Srabani Nanda, part of India's gold-winning women's 4x100m relay quartet at the 2026 Asian Relays Championships in Shangyu, China.
sports.nri_angle: Indian athletics has rested almost entirely on Neeraj Chopra's javelin; a women's sprint relay gold won by beating host China broadens that story with new names, just weeks before the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and with India set to host the next Asian Relays in Chandigarh in 2027 — a fresh rallying point for NRIs invested in India's Olympic ambitions.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Rishabh Pant Is Going Home to Delhi — and He Took a 12-Crore Pay Cut to Get There
sports.excerpt: The IPL has confirmed the season's biggest trade: Pant returns to Delhi Capitals for INR 15 crore while Kuldeep Yadav heads to Lucknow, unwinding the record deal that made Pant the most expensive cricketer in the league's history.
sports.image_caption: Rishabh Pant, who returns to Delhi Capitals in the IPL 2027 trade window after two seasons with Lucknow Super Giants
sports.nri_angle: The IPL is the diaspora's loudest shared spring ritual, and Pant's pay-cut homecoming to Delhi — days after NRIs celebrated his Headingley century — is exactly the kind of franchise drama Indians abroad follow as closely as any match.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Fifteen Golds in Mersin: India's Young Para-Shuttlers Just Announced the Next Generation
sports.excerpt: India finished the 2026 World Abilitysport Youth Games in Türkiye with 27 para-badminton medals — 15 of them gold — spread across every classification, a haul that points to a pipeline far deeper than its Paralympic stars alone.
sports.image_caption: Indian para-badminton international Mansi Joshi in 2020 (file photo); India's youth squad won 27 para-badminton medals in Mersin
sports.nri_angle: India's para-badminton has become a global powerhouse, and this youth haul signals the next generation — a point of pride for NRI families raising children in inclusion-focused Western systems and a sign that the pathway in para-sport now exists in India too.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Lose Another All-Rounder Before England — and Hand a Mumbai Newcomer His First Cap
sports.excerpt: Nitish Kumar Reddy has been ruled out of India's T20I tours of Ireland and England with a quadriceps injury, and the selectors have responded by drafting in the uncapped Mumbai all-rounder Suryansh Shedge for his maiden call-up.
sports.image_caption: India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, ruled out of the Ireland and England T20Is with a quadriceps injury
sports.nri_angle: India's Ireland and England white-ball summer is the most accessible tour for UK and Irish NRIs in years, and the all-rounder reshuffle — Reddy out, Pandya out, an uncapped Mumbai name in — will directly shape the XI diaspora crowds see at Belfast and English grounds.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Eleven Balls: A 15-Year-Old Just Broke the Fastest-Fifty Record in 50-Over Cricket
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi reached his half-century in 11 deliveries for India A against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla, the quickest in the history of List A cricket — a record-breaking innings of 94 off 29 days before the teenager is set to become India's youngest ever men's international.
sports.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old who hit the fastest fifty in List A history
sports.nri_angle: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the prodigy the entire cricket-following diaspora is tracking — his record 11-ball fifty comes just as he is named for India's tours of Ireland and England, putting a likely record-breaking debut within reach of NRI crowds and making him the must-watch name of the summer.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Five Hundreds Were Not Enough: England Chase 371 at Headingley, and India's New Era Opens With a Defeat
sports.excerpt: Ben Duckett's brilliant 149 carried England to 373 for 5 and a five-wicket win on the final day, leaving India the first team in Test history to lose a match in which it scored five individual centuries — a chastening start to Shubman Gill's captaincy.
sports.image_caption: Ben Duckett, whose 149 powered England's chase of 371 at Headingley
sports.nri_angle: A new India era under captain Shubman Gill — the first Test of the post-Kohli, post-Rohit transition — opened with a wrenching defeat despite five individual centuries. For the large British-Indian crowd at Headingley and NRIs watching across the US, Canada and the Gulf, it was a sobering, unforgettable start to a new chapter of the team they follow most closely.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Oracle Just Told the SEC That AI Cost 21,000 Jobs. India Took More Than Half of Them.
technology.excerpt: The most candid admission yet that AI is replacing tech workers came in a regulatory filing — and roughly 12,000 of the cuts landed in India, where Oracle's largest workforce sits.
technology.image_caption: Servers in a data center, the infrastructure Oracle is spending tens of billions to expand even as it cuts staff
technology.nri_angle: Oracle is the first major tech firm to put AI job losses in writing to regulators, and with India absorbing the largest share, it is a warning shot for every Indian engineer on an H-1B watching the same companies spend on data centers while thinning their ranks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Got Its First 'Sovereign AI' Unicorn. The Twist Is Who Wrote the Biggest Cheque.
technology.excerpt: Bengaluru's Sarvam AI raised $234 million at a $1.5 billion valuation — but the lead investor was not a global VC. It was HCLTech, an Indian IT giant betting $150 million on homegrown models.
technology.image_caption: A microprocessor circuit board, the kind of compute infrastructure underpinning India's push to build sovereign AI models
technology.nri_angle: Sarvam's round is the clearest sign yet that India intends to build its own AI stack rather than rent one from Silicon Valley — a shift that reshapes where diaspora engineers and NRI investors place their bets on the next decade of Indian tech.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia Gets the Headlines. But an Indian-Origin CEO Sells the One Chip AI Data Centers Can't Run Without.
technology.excerpt: SiTime, led by Rajesh Vashist, makes the timing chips that keep AI clusters in sync. Revenue jumped 88%, the stock has roughly tripled this year, and inference may need four times more of its product.
technology.image_caption: A close-up of a motherboard and microchips, the kind of precision components SiTime designs for AI data centers
technology.nri_angle: While the diaspora obsesses over Nvidia, an Indian-origin CEO is quietly riding the same AI wave from an unglamorous corner of the chip stack — a reminder that the semiconductor boom NRI investors and engineers are tracking runs far deeper than GPUs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Credit-Card Rewards Founder From Bengaluru Just Got Handed WhatsApp's 3 Billion Users
technology.excerpt: Meta is putting $900 million into CRED and naming Kunal Shah as WhatsApp's first Indian chief. The diaspora's most-used app now answers to a man who built his name on getting Indians to pay their bills on time.
technology.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and FreeCharge, now appointed global head of WhatsApp
technology.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the connective tissue of the Indian diaspora — the app NRIs use to call parents in Pune and run side businesses in New Jersey — and it will now be steered by an Indian founder whose payments instincts point the monetization experiments straight at India first.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Hackers Put Apple and Tesla Trade Secrets on the Dark Web. The Leak Came From a Tata Plant in Tamil Nadu.
technology.excerpt: A ransomware crew claims to have lifted iPhone inspection manuals and Tesla part drawings from Tata Electronics, the company carrying India's bet that it can build the West's gadgets. The breach lands as India races to become Apple's factory floor.
technology.image_caption: A figure surrounded by streaming code, illustrating a corporate data breach
technology.nri_angle: The 'Made in India' iPhone in an NRI's pocket depends on Tata's Tamil Nadu plants staying secure and trusted; a breach exposing Apple and Tesla secrets is a direct test of whether India can be the world's trusted manufacturing base, not just its cheapest one.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Promised Chips for Years. By November, a Tata Plant in Assam Says It Will Actually Ship 48 Million of Them.
technology.excerpt: A state once defined by insurgency is about to become a semiconductor exporter. For a diaspora that has watched India announce fabs and miss deadlines, a concrete shipping date is the news.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of microchips on a circuit board, illustrating semiconductor packaging and assembly
technology.nri_angle: Semiconductor professionals in the diaspora have heard India's chip promises before; the first real export volumes out of Assam are the proof point that decides whether 'return to India' is a serious career bet or still aspirational.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: UPI Was Built So Indians Could Split a Dinner Bill. It Just Went Live at a Paris Department Store.
technology.excerpt: India's payments rail now works in eleven countries, from the Eiffel Tower to a Cambodian street market. For the diaspora, the home-screen app is quietly becoming a passport.
technology.image_caption: A shopper makes a contactless QR-code payment with a smartphone, the everyday gesture UPI is now exporting abroad.
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who fly home no longer need to juggle forex cards or cash across nine-plus countries — the same UPI app on their phone now pays merchants from Paris to Phnom Penh, and the corridor map is expanding toward the markets where the diaspora actually lives.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: An Indian-Born CEO Now Supplies the Memory for Claude — and Has Bought a Slice of the Company That Builds It.
technology.excerpt: Micron's deal with Anthropic ties Sanjay Mehrotra's memory empire directly to a frontier AI lab, days before an earnings report that could show a tenfold jump in profit.
technology.image_caption: A green memory module on a circuit board — the high-bandwidth memory at the centre of the AI build-out.
technology.nri_angle: For NRI investors holding Micron and for the thousands of Indian engineers inside the memory and AI-infrastructure supply chain, the Anthropic pact is a signal that the chip cycle that funds their RSUs has shifted from boom-and-bust to a structural AI build-out — with an Indian-American CEO sitting at the chokepoint.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Cognizant Just Wired ServiceNow's AI Agents Into Its Own. The Indian IT Workforce Is the Experiment.
technology.excerpt: An open-source 'agent orchestrator' lets one company's bots talk to another's. For the millions who staff India's services industry, it is a preview of the job that is being automated.
technology.image_caption: Servers in a data centre — the back-end where enterprise AI agents now coordinate work across platforms.
technology.nri_angle: Cognizant employs hundreds of thousands of Indians and is a top sponsor of H-1B workers in the US; its push to make AI agents do cross-platform enterprise work is a direct signal to NRI techies in IT services about which roles get automated first — and which become more valuable.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Wall Street Asked If Arista's AI Boom Was Over. Jayshree Ullal Just Lifted the Bet to 1.6 Terabits.
technology.excerpt: Arista Networks grew revenue 35% to $2.7 billion as hyperscalers wired their AI data centres with its switches. The Indian-origin CEO is now selling the plumbing for the next wave.
technology.image_caption: Jayshree Ullal, chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks
technology.nri_angle: Arista is one of Silicon Valley's quietest wealth machines for Indian-American engineers and investors, and its fortunes now ride entirely on whether the AI data-centre build-out keeps going.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Every IT Firm Says AI Will Shrink Its Workforce. At Infosys's AGM, Nandan Nilekani Said the Opposite.
technology.excerpt: Infosys sees a $300-400 billion AI-services market by decade's end and plans to keep hiring 20,000 freshers a year — a sharp break from the layoff narrative gripping the rest of tech.
technology.image_caption: Nandan Nilekani, co-founder and chairman of Infosys
technology.nri_angle: For the millions of Indians and NRIs whose careers run through Infosys and its peers, the company is making the contrarian case that AI is a tailwind for IT services jobs, not their executioner.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: For 30 Years India Guarded Its Workhorse Rocket. It Just Decided to Hand the Keys to Private Firms.
technology.excerpt: IN-SPACe has invited private companies to take over the PSLV — the rocket that launched Chandrayaan and 104 satellites at once. Only Indian-controlled firms qualify.
technology.image_caption: An ISRO PSLV rocket lifts off from Sriharikota
technology.nri_angle: India's privatising space sector is opening up to NRI capital and returning engineers just as the global small-satellite launch market explodes — but the Indian-ownership rule sets clear terms for who can play.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married at Home, in His Living Room, With No Cameras. And the Whole Country Can't Look Away.
entertainment.excerpt: On July 5, the most calculated star in Bollywood will quietly marry Bengaluru wellness entrepreneur Gauri Spratt in a registered ceremony — no destination palace, no drone shots, just two families and a superstar who insists he doesn't get the fuss.
entertainment.image_caption: Aamir Khan, who marries Gauri Spratt on July 5, 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: At 20, Priyanka Chopra Turned Down the Bigger Cheque. Twenty-Six Years Later, at Cannes, She Explained Why It Was Genius.
entertainment.excerpt: From a Miss World crown to a Rajamouli epic dubbed in 200 languages, Chopra's Cannes Lions 2026 masterclass revealed the one rule that has governed every brand, film and glass ceiling she's broken — and it hasn't changed since 2002.
entertainment.image_caption: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, who spoke at Cannes Lions 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Dhamaal 4 Blinks First: Ajay Devgn's Gang Sprints to July 10 to Clear the Decks for Nolan
entertainment.excerpt: The OG Dhamaal boys unveiled their trailer off a 60-foot poster cascading down a waterfall, then quietly moved their release a week earlier — because even a treasure hunt knows when to get out of The Odyssey's way.
entertainment.image_caption: Ajay Devgn leads the ensemble of the comedy Dhamaal 4 (Wikipedia)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Sonali Bendre Stopped Chasing the Paycheck. At 51, She's Chasing Something Harder to Buy.
entertainment.excerpt: The '90s sweetheart who survived stage-four cancer now picks roles for purpose, not price — and in a new conversation about success and life beyond the algorithm, she sounds less like a returning star than a woman who has already won.
entertainment.image_caption: Sonali Bendre, the '90s star who returned after surviving stage-four cancer (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Nolan Is Coming to Mumbai. 'The Odyssey' Just Made India a First-Stop on the Map — and Locked Every IMAX Screen in the Country.
entertainment.excerpt: Christopher Nolan, Matt Damon and Tom Holland will walk an Indian red carpet for the first time. The price of admission? Spider-Man doesn't get IMAX, and half of Bollywood blinked.
entertainment.image_caption: Official poster for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey (Wikipedia)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Sunny Deol Holds a Torch, Not a Hand Pump, This Time. 'Batwara 1947' Reunites Him With Santoshi for the Partition Film Bollywood Keeps Avoiding.
entertainment.excerpt: Once called 'Lahore 1947,' Aamir Khan's most ambitious production yet hands Sunny Deol, Preity Zinta and Shabana Azmi a banned Pakistani play — and an Independence Day weekend to break India's heart.
entertainment.image_caption: First-look poster for Batwara 1947, releasing August 14, 2026 (Wikipedia)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Nani Goes Pan-World: The Paradise Will Release in Nine Languages — Including Spanish
entertainment.excerpt: Srikanth Odela's Dasara reunion just unveiled a moustache-twirling Raghav Juyal as villain Vikram Maalik — and a global rollout aimed at audiences far beyond the Telugu-Tamil corridor.
entertainment.image_caption: Nani, who plays Jadal in Srikanth Odela's The Paradise (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ramayana Walks Into Hall H: Ranbir and Yash Eye a San Diego Comic-Con Trailer Drop Beside Marvel and Dune
entertainment.excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's ₹4,000-crore epic is being pitched to the world — a July Comic-Con launch, a TIFF march, and a rumoured Hans Zimmer–AR Rahman concert. The boldest flex Bollywood has tried in a decade.
entertainment.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Ramayana (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: 16 Celebs, One Underground Bunker, Zero Loyalty: Kunal Kemmu's 'Alliance' Is Prime Video's Most Ruthless Game Yet
entertainment.excerpt: It premieres June 26 in 240 countries at once — the first time Prime Video has gone global with an Indian unscripted format. The catch? The whole thing is built on a lie.
entertainment.image_caption: Kunal Kemmu, host of Prime Video's reality series Alliance (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: Couture, Crystals and a Whole Lot of Attitude: Inside Bollywood Hungama's Style Icons Summit 2026
entertainment.excerpt: Vaani Kapoor, Nawazuddin Siddiqui, Pooja Hegde and a small army of OTT's most-watched faces turned a Mumbai daylong fashion summit into the year's most opinionated red carpet.
entertainment.image_caption: Vaani Kapoor at the Bollywood Hungama Style Icons Summit and Awards 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: "Sita Aaj Lanka Khud Jalane Aayi Hai": The Alpha Trailer Hands the YRF Spy Universe to Two Women — and a Hrithik Cameo Lit the Fuse

lifestyle-health.title: Lifting Weights Just an Hour or Two a Week Is Linked to a Longer Life, a 30-Year Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking nearly 150,000 people for three decades, researchers found a clear sweet spot — about 90 to 120 minutes of strength training a week — tied to lower death rates, with the biggest gains against heart disease and dementia when weights were paired with everyday aerobic activity.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 30-year study of nearly 150,000 people links one to two hours of weekly strength training to a longer life
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Strength training is still rare in many Indian and South Asian households — walking is the default, the gym is seen as vanity, and women in particular are often steered away from weights — yet this is precisely the community that carries an outsized burden of diabetes and heart disease that building muscle helps blunt.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Aging Doesn't Have to Mean Decline — Nearly Half of Older Adults Got Sharper or Stronger, a Yale Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking more than 11,000 older Americans for over a decade, Yale researchers found that 45 percent improved in memory, mobility, or both — and the people most likely to gain were those who held a more hopeful view of growing old.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new Yale study finds nearly half of adults over 65 improved in memory, mobility, or both — with a hopeful view of aging a key factor
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many Indian diaspora families care for ageing parents and grandparents across continents, and the cultural script of later life is often one of inevitable frailty and dependence; this study suggests that mindset itself shapes how elders age — a reason to treat older relatives as capable of growth rather than quietly writing off their decline.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One Question — 'How Old Do You Feel?' — May Reveal Whether You're Sleeping Well Enough
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study of more than 3,100 adults finds that people who feel older than their actual age tend to sleep worse, pointing to a single, disarmingly simple cue that something may be off with your rest.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study links feeling older than one's age to poorer sleep, offering a simple self-check on whether the body is getting enough rest
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Sleep is the quiet casualty of immigrant life — long commutes, late shifts, calls timed to family in India, and the grind of building a life in a new country all erode it; this research hands the diaspora a free, instant self-check on whether that chronic rest deficit is catching up with them.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Lifting Weights, Not Just Walking, May Be the Missing Piece in Holding Off Diabetes
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking nearly 144,000 adults for almost two decades, researchers found that regular strength training cut the risk of type 2 diabetes — and pairing it with aerobic exercise and less screen time cut that risk by more than half.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new 144,000-person study links regular strength training, alongside aerobic exercise, to a sharply lower risk of type 2 diabetes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop type 2 diabetes earlier, at lower body weights, and at far higher rates than most populations — yet exercise in many diaspora households still means a walk, if anything, with strength training seen as optional or vain; this study reframes resistance work as a core piece of prevention for the community most at risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much Fat You Eat, but Which Kind — a Diabetes Review Shifts the Blame
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scientists reviewing the molecular evidence argue that palmitic acid, common in palm oil, fried food and baked goods, quietly sabotages insulin, while the oleic acid in olive oil and nuts may shield against it — pointing to fat quality, not quantity, as the real lever.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new review argues the type of fat — olive oil's oleic acid versus palm oil's palmitic acid — matters more than the amount for diabetes risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Palm oil and reused frying oil are everywhere in the Indian diaspora's kitchens and takeaways — in packaged snacks, sweets, namkeen and restaurant fryers — making palmitic acid an unusually heavy presence in desi diets already burdened by sky-high diabetes rates; this review suggests swapping the oil, not just cutting the fat, could matter more than calorie-counting.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Hardest Part of Losing Weight Is Keeping It Off — a New Review Says Exercise Is the Glue
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Pooling 11 clinical trials, researchers found that people who kept exercising after losing weight regained nearly three kilograms less than those who stopped — a small but remarkably consistent edge in the war against the rebound.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new meta-analysis finds staying active after weight loss helps prevent the kilos from creeping back
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Crash diets and quick weight loss before a wedding or a trip home are a familiar ritual in many Indian families — and so is the quiet return of the kilos months later; this review reframes the goal from losing weight to defending it, a message that matters for a diaspora facing high rates of diabetes and heart disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Mother's Heart Health Before Birth May Shape Her Child's Development, a Study of 8,000 Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Children of mothers with poor cardiovascular health had a 62% higher risk of developmental delay by age four — across communication, movement, problem-solving and social skills — pointing to pregnancy as one of the earliest windows to protect a child's future.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 8,000 mothers links poor cardiovascular health in pregnancy to higher developmental-delay risk in children
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian women carry unusually high rates of gestational diabetes, high blood pressure and heart disease, often undiagnosed, while pre-pregnancy health is rarely discussed in diaspora families fixated on the baby rather than the mother; this research makes a mother's own heart health a quiet but powerful lever over her child's lifelong development.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Simple Walk With Poles Eased Depression in Five Weeks, a New Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a randomized study of 64 adults with moderate-to-severe depression, a supervised Nordic-walking program brought large, rapid drops in symptoms within the first five weeks — and the most severely depressed improved the fastest.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new randomized trial found supervised Nordic walking eased moderate-to-severe depression within five weeks
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Depression is heavily stigmatised and under-treated across many Indian families, where therapy and antidepressants are still met with shame or silence; a low-cost, group-friendly walk that shows benefit in weeks is the kind of accessible, face-saving first step that can reach diaspora elders and stressed newcomers who would never walk into a psychiatrist's office.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It Isn't Just the Calories: Ultra-Processed Diets Are Now Linked to Falling Male Fertility
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A tightly controlled feeding study found that just three weeks on an ultra-processed diet worsened body fat, blood lipids and hormones tied to sperm production — even when calories and nutrients were matched — pointing the finger at industrial processing itself.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A controlled study links ultra-processed diets to hormonal changes affecting sperm production in young men
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Falling fertility and rising reliance on packaged convenience food are both acute in diaspora life — long work hours, ready meals and Western supermarket aisles displacing home-cooked dals and vegetables — making this a quietly personal warning for younger NRI couples already navigating the cost and stress of fertility treatment abroad.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A High-Dose Omega-3 Pill Reached the Brain but Did Nothing for Memory, a Gold-Standard Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a two-year randomized trial of older adults at risk of dementia, daily fish-oil-style DHA more than doubled omega-3 levels in the blood and reached the brain — yet it failed to improve memory, thinking or the size of the brain’s memory centre any more than a placebo.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Omega-3 fish-oil capsules; a two-year randomized trial found high-dose DHA reached the brain but did not improve memory
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Fish-oil and omega-3 capsules are among the most popular over-the-counter supplements in Indian-origin households, often bought in bulk and taken for years in the belief they protect the aging brain; this rigorous trial is a reminder that for most people the money may be better spent on diet and exercise than on a daily pill.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much Protein You Eat, but Which Building Blocks — a New Longevity-Diet Study Suggests
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scientists at USC report that fine-tuning a single amino acid, methionine, let mice eat more food yet lose fat without losing muscle — and that people eating the most animal protein had twice the rate of diabetes, hinting the kind of protein may matter more than the amount.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Lentils and legumes; new research suggests the type of protein, not just the amount, may shape metabolic health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The protein debate cuts to the heart of diaspora eating habits — from the dal-and-rice plant-based traditions of many Indian households to the high-protein, meat-heavy regimes popular in Western fitness culture — and this research suggests the traditional emphasis on plant proteins may carry an underappreciated metabolic advantage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Joint-Pain Supplement Millions Take May Quietly Speed Up Alzheimer’s, a New Study Warns
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study in Nature Metabolism finds that glucosamine — one of the world’s most popular supplements for aching knees — fuels a sugar build-up in the brain that worsened memory in mice and was tied to faster decline and higher death rates in people with dementia.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Dietary supplement capsules; a new study links glucosamine to a sugar build-up that worsened Alzheimer’s in mice and people
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Glucosamine is a staple in the supplement cabinets of older Indian-origin adults managing arthritis and knee pain, often taken for years without a doctor’s oversight; this study is an early but sobering signal that anyone in a diaspora family already living with memory loss should review the habit with a physician rather than assume a 'natural' joint pill is harmless.
